summary: A 60-ft Aermotor erected in 1921 was replaced by a newer tower around 2018 in Centre County, Pennsylvania; current staffing and access are unconfirmed.

events.note: First tower on the site: a 60-foot Aermotor, per Eastern US Lookouts and the register
Debris fire burned the area around the tower; the operator had to leave the tower to avoid smoke (1977 Lock Haven Express report as quoted)
Tower operator on duty in 1977; last staffing record found
Register says the current tower was built circa 2018 as part of the state modernization and replaced the 1921 tower

corrections.proposed: Remove for the current tower; 18.3 m (60 ft) describes the 1921 tower that was replaced
corrections.why: The register says a 60-foot Aermotor built in 1921 was replaced around 2018, and gives no height for the current tower.

corrections.proposed: Aermotor for the 1921 tower only; current tower design not found
corrections.why: The Aermotor design belongs to the replaced tower, not the current structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 1921 and about 2018. They describe different structures on the same site: a 60-foot Aermotor in 1921 and the newer tower around 2018.

notes_for_editor: No source found on current access, current staffing, or the current tower's height and design. Staffing evidence stops at 1977. The 2018 replacement rests on the register alone; the Pennsylvania 2018 chapter report describes the statewide program but does not name Snow Shoe. Status 'standing' is inferred from the register's listing of the current tower; no visit or photo source was read.
